newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London failed to hold on to earlier gains and ended lower. November was $8 off at $1,518 a tonne, while the May contract ended $27 up at $1,445. The July contract rose $10 to close at $1,420. Traders and brokers said there was little reaction to the vice chairman of the National Coffee Council of Brazil comments at the F. O. Licht's Coffee Conference in Hamburg which estimated the country's 1996/97 coffee production at less than 24 million 60-kg bags even though that estimate was at the lower end of the range. In New York the main activity was in the continued weakness in the September contract ahead of its expiry. This dragged down the rest of the board as well. The spot September contract, which went off the board today, slid 3.00 cents/lb to finish at 109.20 cents. September's premium to second-position December continued to shrink, falling to 4.80 cents/lb, compared to 6.35 cents/lb at the close Tuesday. December ended 1.45 cents/lb lower, at 104.40 cents/lb, while the back months closed between 0.50 to 0.65 cent/lb lower. Traders said that there is still downside potential, although a free fall is not expected because of the low level of consumer stocks, which could help stabilize the market.

UNITED STATES - The United States imported 1.460 million 60-kg bags of coffee in July 1996, nearly 20 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 11.521 million bags, 16 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose to 17.1 million bags up from 16.2 million bags in 1994 but down on the 1993 figure of 19.3 million bags.

SWITZERLAND - Switzerland imported 90,354 bags of coffee in July 1996, 2.9 percent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of January 1996 up to 661,900 bags, 11 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 9.5 percent to 1.048 million bags. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Uganda (58,200 vs 19,900 bags), Costa Rica (58,700 vs 71,000 bags) and Colombia (84,400 vs 57,700 bags). The country exported 146,700 bags of coffee in January/July 1996, significantly up on last year's figure of 91,000 bags. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 5.9 per cent to 184,500 bags.

BRAZIL - Luiz Marcos Suplicy Hafers, vice chairman of the National Coffee Council of Brazil, said he did not expect the 1996/97 Brazilian coffee crop to reach 25 million bags. Speaking at the F. O. Licht World Coffee Conference in Hamburg, Hafers said the real concern was the 1997/98 crop, which needed to be carefully monitored. Hafers said in the following season in 1998/99, the country would make an effort to achieve an output of 30 million bags. He emphasized the world needs 30 to 35 million bags from Brazil, and that the country will do everything to achieve that objective. He said that during the 1996/97 crop the handling of stocks would be decisive for the market, given a local consumption of 12 million bags.
